interpretation: Everything moved by force and contrary to nature is moved by something and by another (255b31-32: τά τε βίᾳ καὶ παρὰ φύσιν πάντα ὑπό τινος καὶ ὑπʼ ἄλλου); this is most evident for things moved contrary to nature (254b24-27). Read per motion: the other moves the thing in the respect in which it is forced. ὑπʼ ἄλλου is read as a per se mover (`MovesIn`), as the thrower, not the wall, moves the rebounding ball (255b27-29).
